title: Ownership
subtitle: What happens with the content you generate on the service?
description: The content and the data you generate on services online is usually subject to copyright law. When your data are collected by services, they can be considered personal data. It means that it is your content, your data: you can decide.

scores.description: The ToS claims ownership of, or assigns to the company title in, the content or personal data generated by the user, stripping the user of their proprietary and authorship rights.
The user nominally retains ownership, but the clause is ambiguous or couples retained ownership with such broad rights granted to the company that effective control over the content is diminished.
The ToS expressly confirms that the user retains full ownership of and title to the content and personal data they generate.

title: Governance
subtitle: Your relationship with the service and the community
description: description

scores.description: The company retains wholly unilateral and discretionary governance over the service and its community, with no user participation, published decision-making criteria, or accountability mechanisms.
Some governance structures exist (e.g. published community guidelines or moderation rules), but users have no voice in decisions and enforcement remains at the company's discretion.

The service provides transparent governance with meaningful community participation, such as consultation on substantial decisions, published moderation criteria, and accessible appeal or redress procedures.

title: Guarantee
subtitle: Some services will guarantee you certain features, or explicitly reject any guarantee.
description: description

scores.description: The service is provided "as is" and the ToS disclaims all warranties, offering no guarantee of features, availability or fitness for purpose, contrary to the mandatory conformity guarantees owed to consumers under Article 8 Directive 2019/770.
The service provides qualified or limited guarantees, or disclaims warranties only to the extent permitted by applicable law, preserving the consumer's mandatory statutory conformity rights.
The service expressly guarantees defined features, quality or availability in a manner consistent with, or exceeding, statutory conformity requirements.

title: User Involvement in Changing Terms
subtitle: Are changes proposed as a request for feedback, or imposed unilaterally as a take-it-or-leave-it deal?
description: The terms are a contract between two parties, and it should not be changed unilaterally without consultation of the other party. Services should listen to what their users say and care about, and give them a vote in each substantial change.

scores.description: Terms may be changed unilaterally on a take-it-or-leave-it basis, with continued use deemed acceptance and no consultation of the user, reflecting the unfair term described in Annex 1(j) Directive 93/13.
Users are invited to give feedback or are consulted on some changes, but the company retains final and unilateral discretion to impose them.
Substantial changes require the user's genuine agreement or consultation, giving the user a meaningful vote rather than a unilaterally imposed amendment.

title: Changes
subtitle: Changes to the Terms
description: description

scores.description: The company reserves the right to amend the terms at any time without any valid reason stated in the contract, an unfair term within the meaning of Annex 1(j) Directive 93/13.
The company may amend the terms for reasons stated in the contract, but the reasons are vague, broad, or not all specified, leaving wide interpretive latitude to the company.
Amendments are confined to valid reasons specified in the contract, or the company does not reserve any right to change the terms unilaterally.

title: Jurisdiction and governing laws
subtitle: Where can you sue, or be sued, for breaching of the rules?
description: What is the jurisdiction, what laws govern the terms?

scores.description: The ToS imposes a governing law and/or an exclusive forum other than that of the consumer's habitual residence, contrary to the protection of Article 6 Rome I and the unfair term in Annex 1(q) Directive 93/13.

A foreign governing law or forum is imposed only in relation to businesses, or the clause expressly preserves the mandatory protections afforded to the consumer by the law of their habitual residence.
Disputes are governed by, and may be brought before the courts of, the consumer's place of domicile, or no choice-of-law or choice-of-forum clause is imposed.

title: Notice of Changing Terms
subtitle: Are users notified when terms change? Are they given enough time to find out what changed and discuss this with each other before deciding whether to continue to use the service under the new terms?
description: Services need to evolve. But it is important that updating the service does not break the consentment with the user. Updates and changes to terms of service and privacy policy need to be properly noticed to users and to sollicit their agreement again.

scores.description: Terms may change without any prior notice to the user, with changes taking effect immediately or continued use being deemed acceptance.
Users are notified of changes, but without sufficient lead time or a meaningful opportunity to review the changes and decide before they take effect.
Users receive clear, advance notice of changes with a reasonable period to review them and the ability to terminate the contract before the new terms apply.

title: Suspension and Censorship
subtitle: Can they end your use of the service at any time?
description: Your account and your data are on their servers, so they control them. Which guarantee do you have that lawful content and lawful activity will not be censored or suspended?

scores.description: The company reserves the right to suspend the account or remove or censor lawful content at any time without serious grounds, prior notice, or any possibility of appeal.
Suspension or content removal is limited to stated grounds but lacks a notice period, or includes notice but relies on broad or vague grounds.

Suspension or content removal is confined to serious, specified grounds with a statement of reasons, prior notice, and a right of appeal consistent with Article 17 DSA, or no such right is reserved at all.

title: Business Transfers
subtitle: Is your data a business asset?
description: When you give your data to a company, you need to keep in mind that this company can get acquired by another company, with different policies. What happens in that case?

scores.description: User data may be transferred to a third party upon a merger, acquisition or asset sale without notice to or consent from the user, echoing the unfair assignment term in Annex 1(p) Directive 93/13.
Data may be transferred upon a business transfer with prior notice but without consent, or subject to continuation of the existing privacy commitments.
Any transfer of personal data on a business transfer requires prior notice and the user's ability to object or withdraw their data, or no such transfer is contemplated.

title: Logs
subtitle: How long do they keep them?
description: description

scores.description: The retention period for logs and connection data is undisclosed or indefinite, contrary to the storage limitation principle of Article 5(1)(e) GDPR.
A retention period is disclosed but is lengthy, vague, or not clearly tied to a specified purpose.
Logs are retained only for a clearly stated, limited and purpose-bound period, or are not retained at all and are promptly deleted or anonymised.

title: Security
subtitle: Protecting your account
description: This topic contains all cases which describe the effort of the service to protect your account from unauthorized access.

scores.description: The ToS describes no security measures and/or disclaims all responsibility for protecting the user's account and data against unauthorised access.
Basic security measures are mentioned, but commitments are vague or shift the substantial burden of securing the account onto the user.
The service commits to appropriate technical and organisational security measures and to breach handling and notification, consistent with Articles 32 and 33-34 GDPR.

title: Payments
subtitle: What kind of payment arrangements you will commit to?
description: When you accept the ToS, will you commit to re-occurring payments or automatic credit card charges, does the service require your credit card number, and what kind of privacy implications the payments terms have?

scores.description: The ToS imposes automatic recurring charges or auto-renewal, or stores payment credentials, without clear consent, accessible cancellation, or refund rights.
Recurring payments or auto-renewal exist and are disclosed, but cancellation or refund rights are limited or burdensome to exercise.
Payment terms are transparent, with explicit consent required for any recurring charge and easily accessible cancellation and refund rights, or no payment obligation is imposed.

title: Content
subtitle: What (not) to post.
description: This topic contains all the cases which define what an user is allowed or disallowed to post, publish and discuss.

scores.description: Content restrictions are so broad, vague or discretionary that they unduly restrict lawful expression and permit the company to act arbitrarily against the user.
Content rules are defined but remain broad, leaving significant interpretive discretion to the company over what is permitted.
Content rules are clear, specific and limited to unlawful or genuinely harmful content, with predictable and proportionate enforcement.

title: Copyright License
subtitle: How many rights do you have over your content?
description: Copyright law gives you control over how your content (texts, photos, videos, etc.) can be used, by whom they can be distributed, modified, etc. Sometimes, online services need your permission to perform certain tasks with your content. That's why they ask you to grant them a copyright license. But sometimes, the copyright license is so broad, that your content can be exploited by others without asking you.

scores.description: The user grants a broad, perpetual, irrevocable and sublicensable copyright license that permits the company and third parties to exploit the user's content for purposes going beyond operating the service.
The license is broader than strictly necessary to perform the service, but its purposes are expressly listed and explained, or there is doubt as to whether those purposes are necessary.
Any license is limited to what is necessary to operate and provide the service, or the ToS requires no copyright license beyond that.

title: Trackers
subtitle: How are you tracked?
description:
Covers any technology that allows services to track (identify over time, place, and between devices) a user. These technologies include but are not limited to:

- HTTP Cookies
- IP geolocation
- Browser Session Storage
- iOS Advertising IDs
- Device Fingerprinting
- Data de-anonymization/Data re-identification
- Tracking pixels

scores.description: The service deploys extensive tracking technologies without disclosure, a lawful basis, or any ability for the user to refuse, contrary to Article 5(3) ePrivacy Directive and the consent requirements of the GDPR.
Trackers are disclosed and some consent or opt-out is offered, but non-essential tracking is enabled by default or is difficult to refuse.
Only strictly necessary trackers are used, or non-essential tracking requires freely given, specific and informed opt-in consent that is as easy to refuse as to give.

title: Personal Data
subtitle: Can you control your privacy? Once a service has your personal data, how much control do you have over how it will be used and how long?

scores.description: Once collected, the user has no control over how their personal data is used or for how long it is retained, and the data may be processed for purposes incompatible with those for which it was collected.
Some data subject rights or controls are provided, but they are limited, burdensome to exercise, or retention and purposes are poorly defined.
The user retains meaningful control consistent with the GDPR rights of access, rectification, erasure, restriction, objection and portability, subject to purpose and storage limitation.

title: Anonymity
subtitle: Can you use the service anonymously?
description: The terms sometimes describe the level of logging and the level of data collection and which kinds of data the service is processing. Anonymity or the right to use a pseudonym can be very important for freedom of expression (e.g. for people exercising a certain profession, or people living in authoritarian regimes).

scores.description: The service requires verified real-identity registration, prohibits pseudonymous use, and collects extensive identifying information.
Pseudonymous use is permitted, but some real-identity verification is required, or the data collected exceeds what is necessary to provide the service.
The service can be used anonymously or under a pseudonym with only minimal identifying data, reflecting the data minimisation principle of Article 5(1)(c) GDPR.

title: Types of Information Collected
subtitle: Information the service receives from you
description: What kind of information, whether voluntary or automatically, does this service collect from you?

scores.description: The categories of information collected are not disclosed, or collection is open-ended and excessive relative to what the service requires.
The categories of information collected are disclosed but only broadly or vaguely, or collection exceeds what is necessary for the service.
The categories of information collected are clearly and specifically disclosed and limited to what is necessary to provide the service.

title: User Choice
subtitle: How much can YOU decide?
description: The level of choice that is left to the user.

scores.description: The user is offered no meaningful choices: data use, settings and features are imposed by default with no ability to opt out.
Some choices or opt-outs are provided, but they are limited, defaulted against the user's interest, or difficult to exercise.
The user is given meaningful, granular and easily exercisable choices over how their data is used and how the service is configured.

title: Third Parties
subtitle: "Data Processors", "Social Media Services", "Ad Services"...
description: How much data is processed by external companies? What do these third parties do with a Service? How intrusively is your data handled? This topic summarizes it.

scores.description: Personal data is shared with, or sold to, third parties without disclosure, a lawful basis, or any user control over the sharing.
Third-party sharing is disclosed and limited to stated purposes (for instance, processors acting on the company's behalf), but the user retains limited control over it.
Third-party sharing is minimal, transparent, purpose-bound and subject to the user's control or consent, with no sale of personal data.

title: Right to Leave The Service
subtitle: To avoid lock-in and stay in control.
description: Once you subscribe to the service, will you have the right to leave it and remove your data?

scores.description: The user cannot freely terminate, or cannot delete or retrieve their data and content upon leaving, resulting in lock-in contrary to Article 16(4) Directive 2019/770 and the portability right of Article 20 GDPR.
The user may leave and delete or retrieve some of their data and content, but retrieval or portability is only partial or burdensome.
The user may freely terminate the contract and retrieve and delete all of their data and content, with data portability supported.

title: Law and Government Requests
subtitle: How do services deal with government requests?
description: no text here

scores.description: The service discloses user data to governments or law enforcement without requiring valid legal process, without notifying the user, and without any transparency reporting.
Disclosure is limited to valid legal requests, but the service provides no user notice and no transparency reporting on the requests it receives.
Disclosure is confined to valid legal process, with notice to the affected user wherever lawful, regular transparency reporting, and a commitment to challenge overbroad or unlawful requests.

title: Advertising
subtitle: The ads you see everywhere.
description: How does the service manage your data regarding advertising? How strongly are third parties involved regarding advertising? How much choice do you have on advertising? This topic specifies those kinds of disclosures.

scores.description: Personal data is used for advertising, including profiling and targeting, without disclosure, a lawful basis, or any opt-out, and with heavy third-party involvement.
Targeted advertising is disclosed and some opt-out is offered, but it is enabled by default or relies on extensive sharing of personal data with third parties.
Advertising is non-targeted, or uses personal data only on the basis of informed opt-in consent with an easy opt-out, with minimal third-party involvement.

title: Transparency
subtitle: Transparency and Education
description: The level of information provided by the ‪service that is beneficial (or otherwise) to the user.

scores.description: The terms and policies are inaccessible, unclear, or not drafted in plain and intelligible language, contrary to the transparency requirement of Article 5 Directive 93/13.
Information is provided, but it is incomplete, dense, or difficult to navigate, hindering the user's understanding.
The terms and data practices are presented in clear, plain, accessible and easily comprehensible language that supports an informed decision by the user.

title: Waivers
subtitle: The Rights You Give Up
description: These are generally rights for the consumer that you have under law, but which your agreement with the service takes away from you.

scores.description: The user is required to waive mandatory statutory rights, such as consumer guarantees, the right to bring legal action, or the company's liability for its own breach, terms which are typically void under Annex 1 Directive 93/13.
The waiver is limited, for instance applying only to businesses or only to the extent permitted by law, thereby preserving the consumer's mandatory rights.
No statutory consumer rights are waived, and the ToS expressly preserves the user's legal rights.

title: Dispute Resolution
subtitle: How can be resolved the disputes between you and the service you're using?
description: If a party does something illegal or harms either on a physical or financial way another party, they may start a dispute. The terms of most services set some rules related to dispute resolution, which may negatively affect your rights. Therefore, it is essential to understand what they imply.

scores.description: The ToS imposes mandatory arbitration, a class-action waiver, or a distant forum, depriving the user of access to the ordinary courts, an unfair term within the meaning of Annex 1(q) Directive 93/13.
Alternative dispute resolution is offered but remains optional, or mandatory arbitration applies only to businesses, preserving the consumer's right to bring the matter before a court.
The user retains full access to the ordinary courts of their domicile, with any alternative dispute resolution offered only as a voluntary option.
